- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5), model lags in adjusting; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast 3–5 days ahead.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in 3-day window → reduce forecast sensitivity to recent price moves; apply smoothing factor of 0.85.
